title: Valuing the Money Put Back for a Stopped Catalogue Order
content:
This is the valuation basis on which the money put back onto a Ridgecrest Healthy Options Card for a stopped catalogue order is worked out.

**The amount.** The money put back is what comes back for the order, and never more than the ceiling on what may go back; it is rounded to the nearest cent at the end and at no earlier step.

**Where it goes.** The money returns to the benefit period the order was paid from rather than becoming a fresh allowance.

**The quantities it is built from.**

| Quantity | Its value |
|---|---|
| the value of the items | the smallest order the card's tier will process |
| the delivery charge the order carried | nothing |
| what comes back | the value of the items alone |
| the ceiling on what may go back | the value of the items |

**Worked through on hypothetical figures.** Take a card whose tier will process orders of no less than 8.00 USD. The value of the items is 8.00 USD and the delivery charge the order carried is nothing, so what comes back is 8.00 USD. The ceiling on what may go back is the value of the items, again 8.00 USD, and what comes back does not exceed it. The money put back is therefore 8.00 USD, rounded to the nearest cent once at the end, and it is placed in the benefit period the order was paid from. On a card whose tier will process orders of no less than 5.00 USD the same reckoning gives 5.00 USD.
